title: How a price tag is drawn
summary: A price tag in TCG Card Shop Simulator is drawn from an atlas rather than typed: the game keeps an index for every digit, for the punctuation and the currency marks, for a barcode and a zero, and for each item and object type, and it places each part with its own anchor and colour.
body: A price tag in this shop is drawn rather than written. It is a world interface element with a group and an instanced renderer of its own, which is why a shelf full of tags can be redrawn quickly while you change prices.

Its characters come from an atlas, not from a font. The game keeps a map with an index for each digit, for the period, the comma and a minus, for a space, and for the currency marks it supports: the dollar, the euro, the yen, the pound and the cent.
The same map holds the letters a tag can use. There are cells for p, r, m, s, e and n, a cell for a barcode and a cell for a price of zero, so even the small print on a tag is part of the same sheet.

The map also says how far to advance from one cell to the next, and it pairs item types and object types with their cells. That is why the little picture on a tag can be chosen by what is being tagged rather than being a fixed image.

Colour is part of the tag. It carries a background colour, a colour for the icon background and a colour for the price background, along with a brightness colour and a multiplier for how bright it is.

What appears is switched rather than always drawn. A price, an icon, an amount and a barcode each have a flag of their own, and there is a separate flag for whether a barcode is shown on an instanced tag.

Each part is placed by an offset. The amount and the price each have an anchor offset, the price and the background each have a half size, and the icon is chosen by a cell index, which is how one element can carry a differently shaped tag.

The tag keeps a little state as well. It remembers the price as text and the amount as a value, knows when the price is zero, and has a warning indicator for exactly that case, so a tag reading nothing can look different from a tag showing a real price.
It can also be taken out of culling. A tag that ignores culling is drawn even when the game would otherwise have skipped it, which is a choice the object makes rather than one forced on it.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the atlas sheet with the digits, the punctuation, the currency marks, the barcode and the rows of item and object pictures that a tag is drawn from.
What this entry does not tell you: how many item or object cells the atlas holds, how a price is worked out, or how often prices move. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A price tag is a UI element with its own group and instanced renderer.
The characters come from a map holding an index for each digit, for a period, a comma, a minus and a space, and for the dollar, euro, yen, pound and cent marks.
facts.evidence: identifiers: PriceTagAtlasMap, digitIndex, periodIndex, commaIndex, minusIndex, spaceIndex, dollarIndex, euroIndex, yenIndex, poundIndex, centIndex

facts.claim: The same map holds cells for the letters p, r, m, s, e and n, a barcode cell and a cell for a price of zero.
facts.evidence: identifiers: pIndex, rIndex, mIndex, sIndex, eIndex, nIndex, barcodeIndex, priceZeroIndex

facts.claim: The map gives a cell advance and pairs item and object types with cell indices.
facts.evidence: identifiers: cellAdvance, itemTypeValues, itemCellIndices, objectTypeValues, objectCellIndices

facts.claim: A tag carries a background colour, an icon-background colour, a price-background colour, a brightness colour and a brightness multiplier.
facts.evidence: identifiers: m_BGColor, m_IconBGColor, m_PriceBGColor, m_BrightnessColor, m_BrightnessMul

facts.claim: Showing a price, an icon, an amount and a barcode is switched by separate flags.
facts.evidence: identifiers: m_ShowPrice, m_ShowIcon, m_ShowAmount, m_ShowBarcode, m_InstancedShowsBarcode

facts.claim: The amount and the price have anchor offsets, the price and the background have half sizes, and the icon is chosen by a cell index.
facts.evidence: identifiers: m_AmountAnchorOffset, m_PriceAnchorOffset, m_PriceHalfSize, m_BGAnchorOffset, m_BGHalfSize, m_IconIndexCell

facts.claim: A tag caches the price as text and the amount as a value, and knows when the price is zero, with a warning indicator for that case.
A tag can be set to ignore culling.
A tag holds a reference to the atlas it draws from.
The game ships an atlas for price tags with the digits, punctuation, currency marks, barcode and item and object pictures on it.
